title: A current makes a circular field
hook: Change current magnitude and predict magnetic-field magnitude.
misconception: magnetic-field magnitude stays fixed when current magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply B = μ₀I/(2πr) to compare magnetic-field magnitude when current magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal long straight wire in vacuum observed at fixed perpendicular distance, B = μ₀I/(2πr). When current magnitude doubles, magnetic-field magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model B = μ₀I/(2πr); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal long straight wire in vacuum observed at fixed perpendicular distance, with a nonzero initial result. If current magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on magnetic-field magnitude?
recall.why: Apply B = μ₀I/(2πr) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
